findings.title: Checker still authorizes forged lifecycle evidence and unsafe content
findings.observation: The new contract requires exact durable lifecycle, Git/PR/Review, required-check, external-merge and acceptance authority. The checker instead reads repository-authored JSON and validates field shapes, syntax and reachability. It does not resolve 64-hex message IDs against lifecycle state, query the referenced PR/checks, prove an external merge, or authenticate the asserted acceptance actor. Its own valid Accepted harness fixture uses repeated-digit message IDs, nonexistent PR #42 and Actions run 4242, and an ordinary one-parent empty commit authored by the fixture as merge proof; it still returns PASS. Separately, renderedMarkdown closes a four-backtick fence on a shorter three-backtick line because it stores only the marker character, and the secret regex does not recognize AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.
findings.trigger: A repository contributor commits a syntactically valid authority bundle containing self-asserted lifecycle/GitHub/acceptance facts, hides canonical content behind a longer CommonMark fence containing a shorter fence, or assigns a production-shaped AWS access key.
findings.impact: Each invalid committed snapshot returns exit 0, overall PASS and all 13 checks PASS. The advertised evidence can therefore authorize an Accepted plan without any real Requirements, Review, PR, checks, merge or AcceptanceOwner decision, treat non-rendered records as canonical, or permit a committed production credential. Downstream dependency gates may then trust a forged Accepted state.

evidence.description: The tracked contract states that status changes require exact durable lifecycle, Git/PR/Review and acceptance evidence; arbitrary text, generic URLs and merely well-shaped SHAs are not authority.

validateAuthorityBundle accepts any 64-hex messageId, syntactic PR/check URLs and any reachable commit as merge proof; it never queries durable lifecycle or GitHub and accepts CodeReview decisions APPROVE, READY or MERGED.

The exact-head positive result and supplied 102-case summary reproduce with SHA-256 0c00e95d679538e7aece7080e1cedab2b657eb58144c68a0693f85d0bd167a8c and 6529ddcba2516d3c8e3583491fafb931075cc468c93ab773dc9467869ad53a5b.

The primary suite shows the self-asserted Accepted authority fixture, shorter-fence closure and AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID assignment all receiving 13/13 PASS; summary SHA-256 is 9d1963515c704cb8ec23d112d3fdf492b755936de25d8895a7e6aa5614168170.
Read-only GitHub API probes return 404 for the supposedly valid fixture PR #42 and Actions run 4242; git inspection proves the supplied merge proof is an ordinary one-parent empty commit.
A separate fresh-context pass reproduced the authority failure without reading prior findings; evidence SHA-256 is 91c89b1da1cafc19aaff6bf6d9d2bfabd3af490a77a3eaed83752cb6af4797da.

findings.remediation: Resolve every bundle reference against authoritative state rather than trusting repository-authored assertions: load exact durable lifecycle messages and role routing, query the exact PR/head and required checks, require an externally observed merge whose canonical proof contains the reviewed implementation head, and bind the actual AcceptanceOwner decision. Accept only APPROVE as the CodeReviewResult decision before review-only READY/MERGED workflow proof. Implement CommonMark-equivalent fence delimiter handling and detect AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID plus equivalent terminal credential names with redacted diagnostics. Add each reproduction as an expected failure rather than a valid future state.
findings.verification: At a new exact live head, valid Draft content must retain deterministic 13/13 PASS. A valid non-Draft fixture must be built from real durable lifecycle and GitHub evidence. The forged Accepted fixture, nonexistent PR/check references, non-merge commit, shorter-fence case and AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID assignment must each exit 1 under their intended check without revealing credential values; refreshed PR digests must bind the new artifacts before re-review.
